title: Special Electoral Roll Camps Set for November 21, 22 and 29 in Tamil Nadu
excerpt: Special camps for electoral roll revision will be held at designated locations in Tamil Nadu on Saturday, November 21, Sunday, November 22 and Sunday, November 29, 2026. Voters can get forms and guidance for additions, deletions and corrections ahead of the December 11, 2026 deadline.
body:
• Special camps for electoral roll revision will be held in Tamil Nadu on Saturday, November 21, Sunday, November 22 and Sunday, November 29, 2026, at designated locations.
  • The camps are for voter-list applications — adding, deleting or correcting details — and offer direct access to the necessary forms and guidance, according to Mirror Now.
  • Use Form 6 for inclusion, Form 7 for deletion and Form 8 for corrections, as reported by The Indus Pulse summarising ETV Bharat.
  • Claims and objections remain open until December 11, 2026, ahead of the final rolls on January 4, 2027.

Special camps for electoral roll revision will be held on November 21, 22 and 29, 2026, at designated locations in Tamil Nadu. The Indus Pulse, citing a release reported by Deccan Herald, said the camps will be held on those three dates in Tamil Nadu as part of the 2027 Special Summary Revision. In 2026, November 21 falls on a Saturday, November 22 on a Sunday and November 29 on a Sunday.

Mirror Now likewise reported that the Election Commission will host special camps at designated locations on November 21, 22 and 29, and that the sessions are intended to provide direct access to the necessary forms and guidance for voters before the final electoral rolls are published in January 2027.

Who should attend

The camps are aimed at voters who need to act during the claims and objections period that follows publication of the draft rolls. That includes a person whose name is missing and who needs to seek inclusion, a voter whose recorded details are wrong and who needs a correction, and anyone who needs to raise a deletion or another change to an entry.

The Indus Pulse, summarising ETV Bharat, set out the form for each job: eligible voters use Form 6 to seek inclusion, Form 7 for deletion and Form 8 for corrections. People who will turn 18 on or before January 1, April 1, July 1 or October 1, 2027 can apply for inclusion using Form 6, the report said. Indian citizens living abroad can apply with Form 6A, either in person or by post to the Electoral Registration Officer, it added.

What to bring and what to do

New applicants must furnish the prescribed documents as proof of age and residence, according to the ETV Bharat account summarised by The Indus Pulse. Utility bills for water, electricity or gas that show at least one year of service count as proof of residence, the outlet said. For proof of age, a birth certificate from the local body, municipal authority or the Registrar of Births and Deaths is accepted.

At a camp, a voter can obtain the form for the change they need and the guidance to complete it. Booth Level Officers, Electoral Registration Officers and Assistant Electoral Registration Officers accept the forms on working days, according to the same report. Applications can also be filed online through the ECI Voters' Services Portal or the ECINET mobile application, Mirror Now and The Indus Pulse both reported, so attending a camp is an in-person route, not the only route.

Where the camps fit in the timetable

The camps sit inside a longer revision calendar. Voters have until December 11, 2026 to check their names and details and to file claims or objections. The final electoral rolls for Tamil Nadu are due to be published on January 4, 2027, with January 1, 2027 as the qualifying date for the revision, according to the reports summarised by The Indus Pulse.

For a voter who needs a change, the three camp dates — Saturday, November 21, Sunday, November 22 and Sunday, November 29, 2026 — are the in-person opportunities to get forms and guidance at a designated location in Tamil Nadu before the December 11 deadline. Checking a draft entry first, identifying whether the need is an inclusion, a deletion or a correction, and bringing the age and residence documents described above are the practical steps the reports support.
